body:
Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (4) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. The gate passes checks from the wrong app 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>required_contexts() discards the app_id attached to required checks, and check_checks()
>matches results by context name alone. When a different app reports a successful check with that
>name on HEAD, the gate can pass even though the configured app has not reported its required check.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R2200-2201]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/7/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R2200-R2201) > >```diff >+ req |= set(rsc.get("contexts") or []) >+ req |= {c["context"] for c in rsc.get("checks") or [] if c.get("context")} >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The branch-protection API documents checks[].app_id as the app that must provide the check. The
>new gate retains only context, then computes missing requirements from reported names; neither
>step compares app IDs.
>
> > [room.py\[2194-2210\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/room.py/#L2194-L2210) > [room.py\[2238-2255\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/room.py/#L2238-L2255) > [room.py\[2277-2287\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/room.py/#L2277-L2287) > 🌐 [The `checks` entries include an `app_id` specifying which GitHub App must provide a required check.](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/branches/branch-protection) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Required check configurations can specify a GitHub App, but the gate drops that identity and accepts a same-named result from another app. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[2194-2212] >- room.py[2238-2255] >- tests/test_gate.py[1079-1140] >## Recommended Fix >Preserve each required check's app ID and compare it with the reporting check run's app ID when evaluating required checks. Do not let a same-named result from another app satisfy an app-specific requirement; add a regression test for that case. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/5c879338-59e4-4678-8daf-290e3cf73f0d?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/5c879338-59e4-4678-8daf-290e3cf73f0d)

2. Qodo findings can have two dispositions 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>check_dispositions() adds each Qodo title to seen without rejecting a title already in the set.
>When a dispositions table repeats a finding, both rows can pass validation and the gate reports
>every finding decided despite the conflicting record.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R2143-2147]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/7/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R2143-R2147) > >```diff >+ key = title_key(row["finding"]) >+ if not key and not row["disposition"].strip(): >+ continue >+ seen.add(key) >+ n_qodo += 1 >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The Qodo loop only adds keys to seen, and the subsequent completeness check tests membership
>rather than uniqueness. The cold-dispositions loop explicitly rejects duplicate IDs, while the
>review procedure requires exactly one disposition per finding.
>
> > [room.py\[2140-2159\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/room.py/#L2140-L2159) > [room.py\[2106-2115\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/room.py/#L2106-L2115) > [docs/design/v1.md\[139-151\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/docs/design/v1.md/#L139-L151) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The Qodo dispositions check accepts multiple rows for one finding, so a finding can have conflicting recorded dispositions. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[2140-2153] >- tests/test_gate.py[1-1459] >## Recommended Fix >Before adding a normalized finding title to `seen`, report a disposition error if it is already present. Add a test with two otherwise valid rows for the same archived Qodo finding and assert that the gate fails. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/61970255-b735-4379-b46c-00130509ed8c?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/61970255-b735-4379-b46c-00130509ed8c)
3. An edited hold releases paths nobody approved 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>check_sensitive reads the lead's MERGE-HOLD-<n> text as it stands when the gate runs. It then
>accepts any trusted DECISION-<n> whose comment id is larger than the hold's, but editing a GitHub
>comment keeps its id and parse() never reads updated_at. So if the lead edits an answered hold
>to add a newly matched path, which is what the gate's own "doesn't name X (the form: …)" message
>invites, the old decision passes for a path Matthew never saw. RoomLog.answers has the same gap
>for top-severity owner decisions: an ESCALATION-<n> edited after the decision to name another
>finding makes that decision cover it.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R2408-2411]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/7/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R2408-R2411) > >```diff >+ holds = room.holds(f"MERGE-HOLD-{n}") >+ lacking = [hold_problems(m["text"], a.pr, paths) for m in holds] >+ hold = holds[lacking.index([])] if [] in lacking else None >+ decision = next((d for d in room.decisions(a.decision) if hold and d["id"] > hold["id"]), None) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Hold and decision are compared only by comment id (lines 2411 and 2341), and the hold's paths come
>from its current text (hold_problems(m["text"], …)). The M2 parse() keeps id, created_at and
>text but drops updated_at, so the gate cannot tell when a hold was edited. GitHub comment edits
>change the body and keep the id. The comment at lines 2418-2420 says showing the form is safe
>because a decision must still come after a new hold, but an edit is not a new hold.
>
> > [room.py\[2405-2423\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/room.py/#L2405-L2423) > [room.py\[2324-2341\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/room.py/#L2324-L2341) > [room.py\[203-213\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/room.py/#L203-L213) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The gate links a DECISION to the lead's MERGE-HOLD/ESCALATION only by comparing comment ids. Edited comments keep their id, so an edit made after the decision changes what the decision appears to approve. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[203-213] >- room.py[2324-2341] >- room.py[2405-2423] > >## Recommended Fix >Have `parse()` also return `updated_at` (falling back to `created_at`). In `check_sensitive`, accept a decision only if the hold's `updated_at` is no later than the decision's `created_at`. In `RoomLog.answers`, accept only asks whose `updated_at` is earlier than the decision's `created_at`. When a hold was edited after its decision, say so in the failure and ask for a new hold and decision. Add a regression test where the fake gh returns an edited hold. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/c32315dd-5b03-47a5-bf4d-d13f46f1ba7d?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/c32315dd-5b03-47a5-bf4d-d13f46f1ba7d)

4. An unused room lookup is left behind 🐞 Bug ⚙ Maintainability
>
>Description >
> >
>RoomLog.decision(kind) returns the first trusted decision of a kind, but nothing in room.py calls
>it: check_sensitive and answers both use decisions() with their own ordering rules. A later
>caller could reach for decision() and get a DECISION without the hold and escalation ordering that
>R2-1 and R2-2 added.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R2321-2322]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/7/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R2321-R2322) > >```diff >+ def decision(self, kind): >+ return next(iter(self.decisions(kind)), None) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>A search of room.py finds no .decision( call. The only lookups of decisions go through
>decisions() together with the id-ordering checks.
>
> > [room.py\[2317-2345\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/room.py/#L2317-L2345) > [room.py\[2405-2415\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/624dfffd335be6e2d94b08ff39d8af1b196b6350/room.py/#L2405-L2415) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`RoomLog.decision` is dead code that skips the ordering rules the gate relies on. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[2321-2322] > >## Recommended Fix >Remove the method. If a test uses it, switch the test to `decisions()`. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/12402164-366f-4323-a40b-dd5db6782c59?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/12402164-366f-4323-a40b-dd5db6782c59)

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
